statement: No desktop build of the solo game as Orb plays it exists, and the one workflow that builds desktop programs has never run, would refuse today, and would build main's switched-off data without LAN play.
evidence: ci:gh run list --workflow desktop-builds.yml (no rows, read 2026-11-13)
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; joins three existing pieces (the workflow, the switch stack, the LAN kit's patches)
risk: The joined build differs from what Orb has played; known early by reading the packed data of the first build against the 6a30b4c9 switch list.
orb_question: May the team make desktop test builds for named Alpha testers? Recommended: yes, Windows and Linux.

statement: No Linux build has ever drawn a picture or run on a Steam Deck; the only Linux run on file is a headless one in a cloud container on 9631fc7.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; mostly round trips with a tester who holds a Deck
risk: The Deck's graphics driver may stall or fail on shaders the Windows PC compiles fine; known only at the first real session.
orb_question: Which friend with a Deck will do a first 30-minute session before any Alpha candidate exists? Recommended: ask one now.

statement: LAN play has no Linux build path: the LAN kit exports the Windows preset only, the Linux preset excludes the network code, and the launchers are Windows scripts.
risk: Windows and Linux PCs may part over LAN if any library maths differs; the headless hash match on Linux lowers this but a two-platform LAN match has never been tried.
orb_question: Is LAN play on a Steam Deck part of Alpha, or Windows-only for the first Alpha build? Recommended: Windows-only first.

statement: There is no one-click bench a Deck tester can run that saves a file: the existing kits are Windows batch and PowerShell, and the game's own bench prints to the console only.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable; the old-PC kit is the pattern to adapt
risk: A bench started from a menu shares the tester build's safety lock and must not open a route round it.

statement: Nothing about frame rate, loading or memory has been measured on the build Orb last played, and no windowed native frame record exists for any commit after d7647634 (2026-10-27).
risk: Numbers taken on the shared PC while other sessions run are invalid by the project's own rule.

statement: The frame spikes Orb has felt since 2026-11-01 are still open: two causes were fixed on main but never re-measured, and the building sweep after a blow and the launch tick's slow loops are recorded as not tried.
risk: The launch-tick fixes sit in the sim; if any is not bit-identical the hash moves and it needs a golden window.

statement: No loading time is on file for the desktop game with menus, the tile ground and generated planets; the last native figure predates all three and was already 15 s on a first start.
cost_basis: estimate, no comparable (measuring only; a fix is unsized until measured)
risk: A first start on a Deck compiles every shader cold and may pass 60 s.

statement: Memory has never been measured on a desktop build, and growth over time is marked not measured, so the soak's 10% growth line has no baseline.
risk: A slow leak shows only in a long run; known early by reading memory at 5 and 30 minutes.

statement: The game sets no window: there is no display section in the project file and no fullscreen, resolution, vertical-sync or frame-cap setting in code or in the options.
risk: A change to the project file triggers the full flashing check set (desktop-builds.yml:83-84), so it must be planned, not slipped in.

statement: A build carries a commit and a date but no version number, the Windows program has no icon or version text, and no changelog exists.
risk: Testers report against the wrong build if the number is not on screen.

statement: No tester guide or Deck checklist exists, and the only Deck words (one README line) point to an unpack-and-chmod route a newcomer without a keyboard is unlikely to finish.
risk: A guide written before a real Deck session will be wrong in its steps.

statement: The budget table and its build gate are stale: the Today column is the browser build of e6fa72ff (2026-10-16), the gate is headed proposed, and no frame-time check runs in CI.
risk: Timing on shared runners is noise; only exact counts gate reliably.

statement: Whether stalls crackle the sound on a desktop build is not evidenced: the proven mechanism is the browser build's single-thread audio, and the project's only audio setting is for the web.
risk: None beyond not knowing; one listen in a windowed match settles it.

statement: The desktop workflow builds Windows, Linux and macOS in one job, so a macOS export failure would stop the two Alpha platforms even though Mac comes after Alpha.
ADR 0013 says minimum specs are set before launch with no date, owner or method.
risk: A store page asks for minimum specs before anyone has measured them.

statement: The Windows preset exports a single-file program that runs: a native reading exists for d7647634 and the LAN program of 6a30b4c9 is made from the same preset and passed its loop rows with no script error.
The sim plays the same match on native Windows, the web and a headless Linux binary (one gameplay hash), and on two different processors.
A Linux preset exists (64-bit, data embedded), and the workflow is written to set the executable bit, play the exported binary and compare its hash with the project's.
Plain words for the unsigned-program warning exist for Windows, with Legal's fixed line, in the package README and the LAN readme.
orb_question: Pay for a code-signing certificate so Windows does not warn testers? Recommended: no for Alpha; decide again before the Steam demo.

statement: A long stall or a suspend cannot make the game run hundreds of ticks to catch up: the frame time added per frame is capped at 0.1 s.
Effect shaders are drawn once at start-up, behind the notice, so the first use in a fight does not compile them.
The planet view's per-blow walk of every building, the largest single cause of bursts found on 2026-11-06, is fixed on main with a near-building lookup.
The one-click kit pattern is proven with Orb on a second PC: a double-click, no network, one result file with machine names scrubbed.
Every preset packs the build stamp and the in-game report reads it, so a report can name its build.
Performance's records state the machine's load and mark busy runs invalid, so the numbers on file can be trusted for what they say.
